title: Finite quotient data for a prescribed continuous Galois cocycle
statement: For a field K and the prescribed continuous homogeneous degree-two Galois units cocycle z [def-sc-galois-units-cohomology], its inhomogeneous evaluation c(g,h) [def-sc-brauer-scalar-defect] factors as d(q(g),q(h)) through a locally constant homomorphism q to a finite nonempty group Gamma indexed by Fin n. For all g,h in the absolute Galois group and j in Gamma, d(q(g),q(h)j) g(d(q(h),j)) = d(q(g),q(h)) d(q(gh),j). The displayed multiplication on Gamma is its transported group law, not modular multiplication on Fin n. No normalization is assumed.

source.place: Theorem 03R7 surjectivity and Section 0DVG; explicit regular coefficients and finite Galois descent expanded from the parent construction

proof.text: Write c(g,h)=z(1,g,gh). The iterated continuous homogeneous cochain uncurries by the compact Hausdorff exponential law; evaluation on (1,g,gh) is continuous. Its discrete values give local constancy and finite image by compactness of G squared.

Cover G squared by finitely many clopen rectangles on which c is constant. Refine each resulting finite clopen coordinate partition by cosets of open subgroups: for each point choose a coset neighbourhood in its partition part, take a finite subcover by compactness, and intersect the corresponding subgroup normal cores. Thus there is an open normal N on whose pairs of cosets c is constant. Enumerate the finite nonempty quotient by Fin n, transport its group structure, and let q be the quotient homomorphism. Its coset fibres are open, hence q is locally constant. Define d by values of c on representatives; coset constancy gives c(g,h)=d(q(g),q(h)).

The homogeneous cycle equation evaluated at (1,g,gh,ghr), together with equivariance, gives c(g,h)c(gh,r)=g(c(h,r))c(g,hr). Choose a representative r of the quotient index j; use the factorization and q(hr)=q(h)j, then commute the two unit factors. This gives the stated equation for d. No normalization or division by the quotient order occurs.
